items.abstract_text: ABSTRACT Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly used to explain, summarize, and generate information, yet these activities are rarely framed as reading practices. This conceptual paper examines GenAI‐mediated reading, in which readers engage with responses generated by large language models (LLM) during inquiry and knowledge construction. GenAI frequently presents fluent and synthesized responses whose evidentiary basis, source relations, assumptions, and limitations may remain opaque. This paper identifies three epistemic risks: (a) fluent language may be misrecognized as truth, (b) algorithmic authority may encourage the outsourcing of epistemic judgment, and (c) responsive generation may weaken readers' critical monitoring through confirmation, sycophancy, or automation

items.abstract_text: Abstract Purpose The primary objective of the study was to determine how clinically accurate and useful ChatGPT-4o–generated outputs are when identical prompts are entered simultaneously in 3 independent ChatGPT sessions utilizing the same user-facing model. The secondary objective was to identify whether differences in outputs affect clinical outcomes (ie, impact variability). Methods Five clinical prompts focusing on diabetes management and counseling were developed. Each clinical prompt was simultaneously inputted into 3 separate devices using ChatGPT-4o to generate outputs. Through a modified Delphi technique, 5 clinical pharmacy faculty members with expertise in diabetes management independently rated each ChatGPT-generated output for accuracy (poor, borderline, or good) usefulness (not useful, somewhat useful, or very useful) and impact variability (low, moderate, or high). After initial assessment, responses were collated and anonymously shared among the pharmacy faculty raters. The faculty members were invited to revise their evaluations based on collective feedback, then convened in a virtual panel with moderators to discuss evaluations and work towards consensus. Results Consensus was achieved for all ChatGPT outputs. Accuracy ratings ranged from borderline to good. Two of the clinical prompts yielded outputs that received different accuracy ratings, which may have impacted variability. Usefulness ratings ranged from somewhat useful to very useful, with one clinical prompt yielding outputs that received different usefulness ratings. Conclusion While ChatGPT-4o outputs were generally accurate and useful, limitations and inconsistencies were noted. Users should be aware simultaneously generated outputs across multiple devices using ChatGPT can vary in their accuracy and usefulness in diabetes management.

items.abstract_text: Purpose Artificial intelligence (AI) is vital to healthcare system transformation. Existing research mainly focuses on the macro-level technological empowerment of AI, yet insufficiently explores how healthcare organizations’ strategic commitment to AI translates into better medical service outcomes through individual psychological mechanisms. Design/methodology/approach From the perspective of human-AI collaboration, we utilize survey data collected from medical staff working in Chinese medical institutions to examine the mediating mechanisms and boundary conditions linking organizational AI orientation and AI value co-creation outcomes. Findings Drawing on social cognitive theory, the results reveal that healthcare organizations’ AI orientation is positively related to medical staff’s AI value co-creation outcomes, and AI self-efficacy mediates this relationship. Moreover, their creative self-efficacy positively moderates the relationship between AI self-efficacy and AI value co-creation. Originality/value This study clarifies the micro-level transmission paths between organizational AI orientation and medical staff’s value co-creation outcomes. It provides new insights for hospitals to enhance medical service quality and optimize human-AI collaboration during AI-driven healthcare organizational transformation.

items.abstract_text: Purpose In the AI era, digital transformation has become essential for enterprises to adapt as complex systems to uncertain business environments. In this work, we aim to analyze the evolutionary dynamics of AI-driven enterprise digital transformation (EDT), focusing on its evolution and impact on enterprise performance from a system cybernetics perspective. Design/methodology/approach We employ evolutionary dynamics analysis grounded in game theory to model the EDT process, and perform an econometric and empirical analysis on a sample of Chinese A-share-listed enterprises from 2009 to 2023. The approach encompasses heterogeneity analysis, moderation effect models, such as testing enterprise environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors and market concentration, and threshold effect analyses. Findings The evolutionary dynamics analysis finds that increasing the risk-averse benefits of traditional enterprises and reducing the additional benefit coefficient would hinder EDT. Increasing the investment of technology enterprises in internal resource restructuring accelerates the transformation process. Empirically, AI significantly contributes to EDT. ESG positively moderates the relationship between AI and EDT, while market concentration exerts a negative moderating effect. Furthermore, AI and EDT show an inverted U-shaped trend when R&D intensity exceeds a specific threshold, while a U-shaped trend is observed when enterprise performance exceeds a specific threshold. Originality/value In this work, we uncover the complex, non-linear cybernetic feedback loops, such as U-shaped and inverted U-shaped, and boundary conditions, such as ESG and market concentration for AI-driven EDT, offering systemic strategies for enterprises adapting to the digital ecosystem.

items.abstract_text: The launch of U.S. spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds created an unusual allocation problem: 10 intermediaries offered nearly the same underlying exposure, yet their flows diverged sharply. This paper is a focused reanalysis of the fund-flow and Reddit panel introduced by [Shi, J., Z. Wang, D. Ding, Y. Wang, C. Xia, Q. Ding, and T. Lim, 2026, Who Gets the Flows? AI-Based Brand Visibility, Social Media Sentiment, and Capital Allocation in the U.S. Spot Bitcoin ETF Market, Mathematics, 14, 1959, https://doi.org/10.3390/math14111959]. It does not present the dataset, text measures, BrandScore or the baseline sentiment-by-visibility association as new. Instead, it asks what the established association reveals about the division between category demand and intermediary choice. The contribution consists of three interpretive emphases applied to estimates already reported by [Shi, J., Z. Wang, D. Ding, Y. Wang, C. Xia, Q. Ding, and T. Lim, 2026, Who Gets the Flows? AI-Based Brand Visibility, Social Media Sentiment, and Capital Allocation in the U.S. Spot Bitcoin ETF Market, Mathematics, 14, 1959, https://doi.org/10.3390/math14111959]: within-date differences across funds as evidence about allocation, asymmetry across the conditional flow distribution and variation across market states. The pairwise flow-sensitivity formulation makes the allocation interpretation explicit. In the previously reported two-way fixed-effects model, common daily shocks are absorbed and the sentiment-by-visibility coefficient is identified from differences in issuer visibility among funds facing the same Bitcoin news. The coefficient is positive, the direct visibility effect changes sign between large-redemption and large-creation states and the interaction appears less consistently during stressed markets. The Driscoll–Kraay and issuer-bootstrap checks apply to the baseline coefficient (2.930), not the two-way fixed-effects coefficient (3.802), for which those checks were not conducted. The evidence is thus an associative allocation regularity, not a causal social-media effect: differences in issuer visibility are consistent with different flows across financial wrappers conditional on common category sentiment.

items.abstract_text: Edge AI deployment requires low-latency inference on devices with tight constraints in size, weight, power, and cost. NVIDIA TensorRT accelerates inference through layer fusion, precision reduction, and kernel auto-tuning, but a model containing even one unsupported operator cannot be compiled into a single engine. This paper presents a hybrid TensorRT–PyTorch deployment in which the supported subnetworks run as TensorRT engines while the unsupported operations fall back to native PyTorch, and applies it to an attention-based convolutional neural network (ACNN) whose region-of-interest sampling operators are unsupported. On an NVIDIA Jetson Nano, the hybrid approach reduced the end-to-end latency of ACNN-dsc, the fastest native PyTorch model, from 38.37 ms to 20.40 ms (1.88×) under FP32. Under FP16, the hybrid ACNN-k3 achieved the lowest latency of 17.78 ms, a 2.23× speedup over its PyTorch FP32 counterpart and 2.16× over the fastest PyTorch model. Stepwise profiling of the image preprocessing pipeline showed that transferring raw images and performing most conversions on the GPU more than halves preprocessing latency. Further analyses across devices, precisions, and frameworks show that practical latency on edge AI accelerators depends on hardware and runtime factors beyond FLOPs and model size.

publication_date_provenance.policy: earliest precise publication event; no registry timestamp fallback

items.abstract_text: Summary When a vessel loses propulsion it becomes a drift-dominated casualty, and the response team must begin preparing decisions on towage, refuge, authority notification and specialist salvage engagement before the casualty picture is complete. The information available in the first hour rarely supports the decisions that must be made in the first hour. This paper presents a human-led, staged workflow for early-stage drift assessment and argues that loss-of-propulsion drift should be treated as a defined scenario in the marine operational risk register rather than as an improvised emergency calculation. The workflow makes two contributions: a Stage 0 pre-casualty readiness concept, in which methodology, data sources and escalation logic are prepared in advance; and a staged live process that converts fragmentary, uneven-confidence information into an indicative drift sector and bounded speed band, and connects that picture to response decisions through a decision margin that compares the earliest credible hazard-arrival time with the required response lead time. Drift is estimated by a transparent three-component velocity decomposition with explicit low, base and high scenarios; automatic identification system (AIS) data are used to refine and sense-check the estimate, and artificial intelligence (AI) serves as an organising and consistency-checking layer while technical interpretation and operational authority remain with qualified people. The approach is demonstrated on an anonymised disabled tanker in the northern Arabian Sea, assessed in fallback mode without a pre-prepared Stage 0 readiness file. The initial assessment indicated a drift sector of approximately 119–122°T and a speed band of approximately 0.8–2.0 kn; subsequent AIS movement remained within the broad assessed sector and towards the upper end of the speed band, while exposing the information gaps that pre-casualty readiness is intended to reduce. The case is a single real-condition demonstration, not a statistical validation of the method.

items.abstract_text: Abstract The objective of this work is to demonstrate the successful deployment of a secure, AI-driven closed-loop automation system for LNG plant pre-cooldown. The scope encompasses the transition from a data-driven advisory model to a fully autonomous system that executes real-time valve adjustments. It focuses on achieving critical outcomes in enabling autonomous, real-time adjustments through AI-driven recommendations, minimizing startup duration variability, maximizing additional production hours and reducing greenhouse gas emissions through optimized thermodynamic control. The methodology utilized twenty-five years of historical startup data, which was cleaned and profiled to train supervised machine learning models that predict Main Cryogenic Heat Exchanger (MCHE) temperature profiles and valve responses. These predictive models were integrated with an advanced optimization layer to define precise control sequences that satisfy safe operating envelopes. A cyber-resilient IT-OT architecture was engineered, employing network segmentation and protocol gateways to bridge the plant network and the AI engine securely. The process followed a phased validation: initial deployment as a "live advisory" to calibrate model accuracy, followed by the activation of a closed-loop controller that executes autonomous valve adjustments with human-in-the-loop safeguards. The system was successfully deployed across eight LNG train startups at Malaysia LNG plant. Quantitative results confirm a 16% average reduction in pre-cooldown duration compared to the live-advisory baseline. This acceleration directly translates into increased production availability and the reduction of operators' workloads, which allows operators to focus on strategic overview and process safety —enhancing both safety and efficiency. Observations revealed that the closed-loop implementation successfully standardized the pre-cooldown sequence across all eight production runs, delivering near-identical, optimized cooling trajectories. Critically, the tighter control of the Main Cryogenic Heat Exchanger (MCHE) cooling curve led to a 22% reduction in greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by minimizing flaring events during the transition to stable operations. The study concludes that autonomous closed-loop systems are superior in achieving repeatable, high-efficiency startups. Furthermore, the integration of a secure IT-OT framework addresses the industry's primary barrier to AI adoption: cybersecurity in critical infrastructure. This paper provides a documented case study of an AI system moving beyond "recommendations" into "autonomous execution" in a critical energy facility. It introduces a novel, hybrid methodology combining Supervised Machine Learning with prescriptive optimization logic. This innovation highlights the transformative power of closed-loop, AI-driven automation, reinforcing the organization's leadership in operational excellence and its commitment to setting new standards for industrial processes.

items.abstract_text: Background As Taiwan enters a super-aged society, the prevalence of dementia continues to rise, highlighting the need for scalable, noninvasive approaches to identify behavioral alterations associated with cognitive decline. AI-based analysis of spontaneous affective facial responses has emerged as a potential digital phenotyping tool, but its feasibility for assessing cognitive performance remains underexplored. Objective This study aimed to examine the feasibility of using AI-derived spontaneous affective facial response metrics, including affective expression congruency and onset latency, to characterize differences across cognitive performance levels in older adults with healthy cognition (HC), mild cognitive impairment (MCI), or dementia. Methods A total of 60 participants (HC, MCI, and dementia; 20 per group) were presented with positive and negative emotion-eliciting videos and completed Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) recall and calculation tasks. Facial expressions were video-recorded and analyzed using a convolutional neural network–based AI system. AI-derived metrics included affective expression congruency, categorized as congruent, neutral, or incongruent according to the detected facial response, and affective expression onset latency, defined as the time from stimulus presentation to the emergence of a nonneutral facial expression detected by the AI model. items.abstract_text: We introduce Radial Kernel Attention (RKA) for long-range modeling in polymer machine learning force fields. Local neighbor graphs constrain communication across polymer chains and their surrounding environments, while explicit all-pair attention incurs quadratic cost. RKA maps atomic distances from the cluster centroid to learned radial features and combines their overlap with content-dependent queries and keys. Factorized aggregation and readout enable global feature exchange at linear cost in atom count for fixed feature dimensions. We insert the invariant scalar update between EquiformerV3 local blocks and obtain conservative forces by differentiating the total energy, including its radial coordinate dependence. We evaluate energy and force prediction for finite polymer-derived clusters in OPoly26. Our models are trained on the official training split for 12 epochs and evaluated directly after training on the complete official validation split. A matched 5M comparison shows that RKA reduces per-atom energy and force MAEs by 67.4% and 36.3%, respectively. The 20M RKA model is compared with UMA-S-1.2 and UMA-S-1.2.1 on the same validation structures. The 20M model attains a total-energy MAE of 15.81 meV and a force MAE of 2.619 meV/Å; its per-atom energy MAE is 0.1182 meV/atom. RKA provides a compact global communication pathway that improves energy and force prediction on the evaluated polymer-derived clusters.

items.abstract_text: Subject of Research. This study focuses on the digital banking landscape and the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in private banking and wealth management in Switzerland. More specifically, it examines how technological innovations – ranging from process automation and generative AI to advanced data analytics – alter the operational dynamics, customer relations, and structural competitiveness of Swiss private banks in the context of shifting client expectations and rigorous regulatory environments. Methodology. The research employs a qualitative analytical research design that uses triangulation of secondary evidence. It systematically integrates and cross-checks academic literature on digital finance, fintech adoption and robo-advisory trust, alongside empirical data, regulatory frameworks and market insights from reputable Swiss and international organisations. The primary data sources analysed were supervisory guides from the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA), reports from the Swiss Bankers Association, digital maturity benchmarks from Deloitte Switzerland and private banking market profitability assessments from KPMG and PwC Switzerland. Purpose. The main objective of this paper is to provide a comprehensive assessment of the impact of digital transformation and the deployment of AI on the traditional Swiss private banking model. By analysing seven key dimensions – technological progress, customer expectations, process optimization, data analytics, risk and security, regulation/compliance, and market trajectories – the study aims to clarify the economic mechanisms driving digital adaptation, identify the structural barriers preventing rapid technology adoption, and evaluate the strategic options available to Swiss banks facing intense global competition and margin compression. Findings and Conclusion. The study reveals a significant discrepancy between Switzerland's position as a global leader in asset management, with CHF 9.3 trillion under management, and its digital banking maturity score of 39 out of 60. Although private banking clients continue to establish relationships based on traditional factors such as reputation, trust and personal referrals, they are also demanding friction-free digital execution, personalised dashboards and virtual investment simulations. AI has been proven to have high economic value when acting as a productivity layer centred around advisors, optimising processes such as client onboarding, document extraction, compliance screening and portfolio monitoring. However, it is not as effective when acting as an autonomous replacement for human relationship managers. Ultimately, the integration of digital banking and AI is causing a clear market polarisation. Large-scale institutions are successfully absorbing the substantial fixed costs associated with technology, data governance and regulatory compliance under the frameworks of FINMA and the European Union (such as DORA and the EU AI Act). Conversely, smaller Swiss private banks are under severe pressure to increase their profitability and consolidate, unless they adopt highly focused niche advisory models. The paper therefore concludes that urgent regulatory attention and strategic repositioning are necessary to preserve the overall image and international attractiveness of the Swiss private banking ecosystem.

Objective To investigate how corporate and regulatory actors engineer divergent cognitive realities of AI safety through specific micro-grammatical choices. Methods We proposed an integrated Cognitive-Critical Discourse Analysis framework by synthesizing Langacker's cognitive conception of reality with Fairclough's three-dimensional model, and applied it to a comparative corpus of corporate safety frameworks and regulatory policy documents. Results Tech enterprises engineer a reality of techno-pragmatic containment via active voice, high-certainty evidentiality, and immediate projection to naturalize self-regulation. Conversely, regulatory bodies construct a reality of socio-structural vulnerability using distal modals, passive constructions, and deontic mandates to legitimize state-enforced compliance. Conclusions Linguistic normalization is actively deployed to facilitate or contest corporate epistemic hegemony in AI governance. These findings provide empirical references for revising regulatory discourse and enhancing public media literacy against algorithmic exceptionalism.

After adjustment for GenAI use frequency, the indirect association remained significant, but the small total association was no longer significant. Conclusion The findings highlight effort regulation as a relevant learner-controlled process in the association between GenAI dependency and perceived learning outcomes. Eye movements were recorded, and memory was assessed using signal detection measures (d′) from a recognition task involving target and distractor advertisements. Advertising attitude and product trust were measured using established scales. Results from linear and generalized linear mixed-effects models showed that hyper-salient objects increased early fixation probability and attracted a larger dwell time proportion, demonstrating strong attentional capture. AI-generated endorsers also attracted attention when presented alone, but their proportional attention share decreased when hyper-salient objects were simultaneously present. The effects of these visual elements on memory and product trust were conditional on their co-occurrence rather than uniform across conditions. Within the specific set of experimentally constructed stimuli and four sampled product categories, this research contributes to AIGC advertising literature by developing a visual competition perspective on how multiple AI-generated visual cues interact under limited attentional capacity, offering implications for designing effective generative AI advertisements.

items.abstract_text: Large language models (LLMs) commonly employ key–value (KV) caching to avoid recomputing previous attention states during autoregressive inference. However, its measured performance benefit depends on workload characteristics and the memory environment. This study presents a controlled systems characterization across input context length, model-specific grouped-query attention configurations, and GPU-memory residency. Experiments use Qwen2.5-3B and SmolLM3-3B under verified fully resident conditions with fixed 128-token generation, prompt lengths from 128 to 2048 tokens, randomized cache-enabled/cache-disabled execution, GPU telemetry, and repeated paired validation. End-to-end generation speedup increases from 1.34× to 8.31× for Qwen2.5-3B and from 1.28× to 8.62× for SmolLM3-3B. At 2048 prompt tokens, 30 randomized paired trials confirm mean speedups of 8.10× and 8.51×, corresponding to runtime reductions of 87.65% and 88.25%, while physical GPU-memory utilization remains below 61%. SmolLM3-3B requires twice the theoretical KV-cache storage per token, yet both models show comparable context-dependent scaling in the fully resident regime. Because the models differ in characteristics beyond KV-head count, this cross-model comparison is descriptive and does not attribute the observed performance difference causally to GQA configuration. A separate Mistral-7B case study shows that apparent end-to-end speedup changes substantially under memory pressure; the underlying memory-system mechanism is not isolated. These results establish cache-related end-to-end generation speedup as workload- and system-dependent and demonstrate that meaningful benchmarking requires reporting context length, cache configuration, model and cache footprints, physical accelerator-memory residency, runtime, throughput, and relevant GPU-memory conditions during each inference experiment.

items.abstract_text: BACKGROUND Artificial intelligence (AI) in gastrointestinal endoscopy has focused on computer-aided detection (CADe) for recognition errors; AI addressing endoscope motion, coverage, workflow, and skill – collectively kinematic analysis – has not been systematically synthesized. AIM To map kinematic AI evidence across eight predefined domains and assessed its quality relative to CADe and surgical AI. METHODS MEDLINE/PubMed, EMBASE-OVID, Cochrane, and IEEE Xplore were searched following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses checklist (CRD420261320279). Studies applying AI to kinematic data in gastrointestinal endoscopy were eligible. Risk of bias used Cochrane Risk of Bias 2, Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-2, and PROBAST + AI; certainty of evidence used GRADE. RESULTS Fifty-eight studies were included. Evidence generation was asymmetric: (1) Randomized controlled trial ratio approximately 5:1 (> 40 vs 8); (2) Patient ratio approximately 4:1 (> 27000 vs approximately 6200); (3) Annual publication ratio approximately 12:1; and (4) ≥ 6 vs 0 regulatory approvals favoring diagnostic AI. Withdrawal speed monitoring and coverage/blind-spot mapping reached moderate GRADE certainty, but all 8 randomized controlled trials were from China and 6 of 8 used the ENDOANGEL platform. The remaining six domains have not reached moderate certainty: (1) Workflow recognition and skill assessment are approaching clinical readiness; and (2) Autonomous navigation, robotic control, simultaneous localization and mapping/three-dimensional reconstruction, and instrument tracking remain at the engineering stage. Comparison with surgical AI indicated that the gap reflects ecosystem-level factors – absence of open datasets, benchmarking challenges, and regulatory pathways for motion-acting AI – rather than technical immaturity. CONCLUSION Kinematic AI addresses exposure errors that CADe cannot correct and has shown additive benefit alongside CADe. Two domains are ready for geographically diverse validation; six remain at the engineering stage. Priorities are open datasets, benchmarking infrastructure, and dedicated regulatory pathways for motion-acting AI.

We propose the Human Agency Depth Taxonomy (HADT), a preliminary six-tier taxonomy that classifies the engineering contribution a student makes in a prompt, independent of the AI's output. HADT combines three dimensions: contextual bandwidth, engineering abstraction and student agency. We applied HADT to 962 prompts from 105 students' structured AI Journals in an AI-permissive, first-year software engineering course of 145 students, and examined how agency changed over ten journalled weeks. Most prompts (84.2%) carried some student contribution beyond delegation.

items.abstract_text: ABSTRACT Informatics education requires instructional designs that connect conceptual understanding with procedural application and contextual problem-solving. This study aimed to develop an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-integrated course based on Problem-Based Learning (PBL) to support these two competencies among junior high school students. The product was developed using the Moodle platform by combining digital learning materials, problem-based activities, and AI support in the form of explanations and learning-material summaries. The needs analysis involved 113 students, while the learning-outcome evaluation employed an experimental group and a control group, each consisting of 34 students, using pretests and posttests. The needs analysis revealed percentages of 23% for decomposition, 50% for pattern recognition, 35% for abstraction, and 44% for algorithms. In procedural application of computational thinking, the experimental group's mean score increased from 58.40 to 82.60, whereas the control group's mean score increased from 57.90 to 70.30. For contextual problem-solving, the experimental group's mean score increased from 56.80 to 83.10, while the control group's mean score rose from 57.20 to 71.40. Descriptively, the experimental group demonstrated greater improvement in both measured competencies. These findings indicate the potential of the developed AI-integrated PBL course to support Informatics learning; however, its statistical effectiveness must be confirmed through inferential testing. items.abstract_text: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is changing the environment of language learning, but its theoretical basis and ethical boundaries have not been fully explored. This paper builds a multi-level analytical system for AI-assisted language learning based on cognitive load theory, the zone of proximal development, generative linguistics and the technology acceptance model. AI can help students learn better by reducing extraneous cognitive load and providing easy-to-access support and instant correction; however, due to technological limitations, it may also reduce students' sense of ability and self-management. Generative linguistics and generative AI are not in opposition; rather, the former advocates for data frugality and innate mechanisms, while the latter is characterized by data maximalism and statistical learning; they are in harmony at the level of third factors and the Minimalist Program. According to the above research, chatbots have shown a modest positive effect on language learning; this degree varies depending on the learner's level, interface Design, interaction characteristics, etc. Based on the above, this paper introduces a "Smart Chinese" collaborative learning plugin that integrates ChatGPT with special scaffolding tools for assessment, planning, practice, feedback and community support. Finally, it presents the ethical problems of algorithmic bias, data privacy, over-reliance, and educational gaps, and proposes a multi-level governance system at the institutional, technological and pedagogical levels.

This study examined the impact of media convergence on the behaviour and attention span of adolescents in selected secondary schools in Rivers State, Nigeria. Employing a survey research design, data were collected from 330 students across three secondary schools using structured questionnaires and teacher interviews. Findings indicate that 60% of respondents reported high daily exposure to online media, with the majority acknowledging that media use affects focus, reduces study time, and influences classroom behaviour. The results highlight a significant relationship between prolonged media exposure and decreased attention span, increased distractibility, and altered behavioural patterns. The study concludes that while digital media can enhance learning opportunities, excessive exposure poses risks to adolescents’ cognitive development and academic performance. Recommendations include strengthening digital literacy education, implementing screen-time regulations, and promoting balanced media use in schools. The findings provide valuable insights for educators, parents, and policymakers seeking to mitigate the adverse effects of media convergence on adolescents.

GAI-PE cut task time by 44.2 per cent against HT and by 17.1 per cent against NMT-PE. Its MQM scores were higher than those of NMT-PE, while the difference from HT did not reach significance. Pupil diameter change was nevertheless largest in GAI-PE at 0.095 mm, against 0.083 mm in HT and 0.064 mm in NMT-PE, while gaze on the source text fell to 38.3 per cent, the lowest of the three. Subjective ratings moved the other way and ranked HT as the most demanding condition. In an exploratory analysis, self-reported AI-use frequency was associated with a smaller pupil response in GAI-PE, whereas English proficiency showed no such association. Research follows the female protagonist of the film, named Nehma, an Indigenous (Adivasi) woman who works as a data labeller. Her deep, traditional knowledge about nature is ignored because of the way AI categorisation systems use a rigid, one-size-fits-all sorting method and act as epistemic hierarchies that erase Indigenous ways of living and thinking. Using a social semiotic approach, the research identifies a disconnection between local ecological knowledge and the rigid binary logic of machine-learning infrastructures. The article argues that digital frameworks mirror power dynamics inside educational institutions, where underrepresented students often have their cultural identity and cultural expressions erased or misrepresented. By analysing the lived experiences of marginalised communities, the study critiques techno-solutionist solutions and proposes solutions grounded in epistemic justice, cultural agency and equity and recommends that equitable AI systems require moving away from extractive labour practices to recognise the intellectual and cultural contributions of the Global South.

items.abstract_text: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) tools have made their way into English Language Teaching (ELT) contexts, yet their pedagogical value remains contested. While many learners engage with GenAI primarily as a quick hack for producing answers, fewer use it as a resource for reflective language learning. This study explores prompt writing as a language learning task that supports both language development and metacognitive awareness. The study was conducted with a target group of pre-seminary, tertiary-level learners with mixed linguistic proficiency. Over the course of four instructional sessions, the study used a classroom-based action research design. Learners engaged in cycles of prompt drafting, GenAI-generated responses, peer discussion, and prompt refinement. Classroom observations, learner reflections, and group discussions were used to gather qualitative insights. The findings indicate measurable improvement in learners’ autonomy, as learners became aware of how lexical choices shape meaning, along with increased engagement, teamwork, and reflective thinking. The study argues that prompt writing, when treated as a language task rather than a technical skill, can function as a practical tool for fostering metacognition in ELT classrooms.

items.abstract_text: Today, Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is quickly becoming a staple of university students' work, as it can provide instant answers to information search, writing, explanation and problem solving. While GenAI can aid in learning, overreliance can lessen students' independent thinking. This study explores the ties between generative AI reliance and students' problem-solving skills, focusing on cognitive offloading as a mediation factor and AI literacy as a moderation factor. A quantitative, cross-sectional research design is suggested with a sample of 100 University students. The data will be analyzed using descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, Pearson correlation, regression, mediation and moderation analysis through SPSS. The conceptual model suggests that students' problem-solving ability may be linked to their degree of cognitive offloading, which could be further linked to their reliance on GenAI. The authors suggest AI literacy as a boundary condition that could affect the relationship between GenAI dependence and problem solving ability. New studies suggest that students' use of GenAI in problem-solving is multi-layered and constructive, as well as thoughtless, and that there are four aspects of AI literacy: knowledge, application, evaluation, and understanding of ethical issues. Thus, the present study is centered on not only students' usage of GenAI, but also how reliance on GenAI can impact their thinking processes when addressing academic challenges.

items.abstract_text: The article develops a psycholinguistic account of how generative artificial intelligence changes professional Ukrainian-language writing, with particular attention to language norms, professional speech etiquette, communicative culture, and the educational workplace. A structured theoretical synthesis was conducted on a corpus of 29 peer-reviewed journal articles from 2022–2026. The corpus was organised into four evidence blocks: artificial intelligence in business and workplace communication; pragmatic behaviour of large language models; politeness and email communication in academic and workplace settings; and Ukrainian psycholinguistic and speech-etiquette contexts. Studies were coded for communication domain, speech act or genre, role of artificial intelligence, normative and pragmatic outcomes, relational perceptions, and contextual limitations. Because research designs and outcome measures were heterogeneous, the analysis used qualitative comparative synthesis rather than meta-analysis. The synthesis reveals three recurrent transformations. First, generative systems often strengthen formal correctness, structural coherence, and explicit politeness. Second, these gains can be accompanied by communicative conventionalisation: increased formality, formulaic organisation, reduced lexical or strategic variability, and weaker adjustment to the local interpersonal context. Third, artificial-intelligence mediation changes attributional and relational judgements: perceived authorship, authenticity, sincerity, trust, and willingness to maintain interaction may diverge from ratings of professionalism or clarity. These transformations are not uniform; their magnitude depends on communicative risk, status relations, degree of imposition, genre conventionality, source disclosure, and the extent of human revision. On this basis, a three-component model of normative optimisation, communicative conventionalisation, and attributional-relational shift is proposed. For Ukrainian professional communication, especially in higher education, generative artificial intelligence should be treated as a mediator of linguistic choice rather than a neutral editing device. The key research gap is the lack of direct empirical evidence on Ukrainian-language AI-mediated professional writing, which limits straightforward transfer of findings from English-dominant studies.
